notes: v1.14.577 — A GATE THAT CANNOT BE ANSWERED NOW SAYS SO. FIRST-DOOR Ship A slice A-4, the last one, and the fix board v2 Q-1 asked for: an indeterminate state, NOT removing the ring. THE DEFECT, PRECISELY: the readiness gate No open blockers was !(blockerCount > 0), which is TRUE when there is no deployment at all - zero blockers of zero racks. A phone with nothing set up read 25%, one gate of four passing on a question the app had no standing to answer. That is a gauge that lies, and it lied in the most flattering direction. null IS THE THIRD STATE AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT false. False means there IS an open blocker - a job to do. null means there is nothing here to have blockers yet - no job and no claim. Collapsing the two would have traded a flattering lie for a discouraging one. ONLY THIS GATE CHANGES, and the asymmetry is the point rather than an oversight. Handoff started is also false with no deployment, but false is HONEST there: the shift genuinely has not been handed off. Only the blockers gate claimed a PASS it had not earned. THE DENOMINATOR IS THE ANSWERABLE GATES, NOT ALL FOUR. Scoring an unanswerable gate as a MISS would be the opposite lie - the app reporting a shortfall against a question it never asked. The count line now names its own denominator and says how many are not applicable yet, so the number and the reason arrive together instead of the technician inferring one from the other. NO NUMBER AT ALL WHEN NOTHING IS ANSWERABLE: the ring reads an em dash rather than 0%, because 0% reads as measured-and-failing while the truth is not-measured. THE INDETERMINATE ROW IS NEVER warn. warn is the attention channel and means a technician must do something; an unanswerable gate asks for nothing. It renders an em dash, muted, with a title that says why - keeping the attention channel meaning one thing, per the .323 colour lock. NOT IN THIS SHIP: Ship A is now complete through row 9. FIRST-DOOR Ship B has not started, and INTEL-DOCK and SITE-SYNC remain sequenced behind it.
